newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin arrives in Kremlin to see Chernomyrdin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin arrives in Kremlin to see Chernomyrdin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin went to the Kremlin on Tuesday and will meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin there, the presidential press service said.
Yeltsin, 66, is recovering from pneumonia at an official residence outside Moscow, but he has paid a handful of visits to the Kremlin since he left hospital.
Television film of these visits and of other meetings shows that he has aged since he was taken ill with heart problems last year and with pneumonia last month.

Yeltsin's doctors have advised him not to rush back to full-time work, although Chernomyrdin said an interview published in the Washington Post on Tuesday that Yeltsin was unlikely to follow the advice.
"He is tired of these doctors," Chernomyrdin said.

The two men, who meet most Tuesdays, are due to discuss Chernomyrdin's planned visit to the United States later this week, which will in turn prepare the ground for a summit meeting between Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton.
The summit was originally scheduled for Washington, but Chernomyrdin told the Washington Post he favoured shifting it to Europe to conserve Yeltsin's strength.
The Kremlin said on Monday that Yeltsin planned only a few meetings this week and would work on an address due to be delivered to both houses of parliament later this month.
